description: p-limit limitFunction: PromiseLike-returning fn + Options in, Promise-returning fn with clearQueue out (type-level)
type: project
---
In the p-limit project at /work/p-limit, the explicitly remembered public contract of the exported `limitFunction` is its declaration in `index.d.ts`: `function_` must be `(...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType>` (a PromiseLike-returning function; no plain non-Promise sync return is declared acceptable) and `options` is the `Options` object, and it returns `((...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>) & Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue'>` — the returned function carries only `clearQueue` from `LimitFunction` in its declared type.

This is a type-level restriction from the inspected declaration, retained for future maintenance; it is not proof of runtime enforcement. Note the Promise/PromiseLike distinction: the input contract is `PromiseLike<ReturnType>` while the output returns `Promise<ReturnType>`. The declaration by itself does not establish that any named test passed.

description: p-limit's package.json test script is "xo && ava && tsd"; tsd type-checks reject limitFunction on a sync-returning function
type: project
---
The inspected `package.json` of the p-limit project at /work/p-limit defines `"test": "xo && ava && tsd"`, so a test run also executes tsd type declarations checks. The tsd file `index.test-d.ts` contains `expectError(limitFunction((_a: string) => 'x', {concurrency: 1}));`, i.e. the tsd type check expects a sync-returning (non-PromiseLike) function to be rejected as `limitFunction` input at the type level. `index.test-d.ts` imports `expectType`/`expectError` from tsd.

entries.content:
---
description: p-limit test.js gates rejectOnClear/clearQueue tests with test.skip only when process.versions.node starts with '20.'
type: project
---
In the p-limit project at /work/p-limit, `test.js` conditionally selects the runner: `const testClearQueueRejects = process.versions.node.startsWith('20.') ? test.skip : test;`. The tests `clearQueue rejects pending promises when enabled` and `limitFunction exposes clearQueue` are declared with `testClearQueueRejects`, so they are skipped only when the Node version string starts with `20.`; on other Node versions the same tests run, and in the observed run `clearQueue rejects pending promises when enabled` executed and passed. A preceding source comment says "Node.js 20 has a bug where DOMException is not properly handled by AVA's `throwsAsync`" — that is what the source states as its rationale, not an independently verified Node.js defect.
entries.description: p-limit test.js gates rejectOnClear/clearQueue tests with test.skip only when process.versions.node starts with '20.'
